sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog: resources in and about the Middle Watut language (mpl), up to date 2025-11-04; item records oai:sil.org:62834 and oai:sil.org:85273
sources.note: Bibliographic only. 'Language descriptions' facet lists nothing but Glottolog and the Midkiff 2019 dictionary; no OPD or phonology write-up exists for Middle Watut in any OLAC archive. Also lists Torro 2009 Tsangg trilingual dictionary (SIL 62834, 'orthography design' workshop), Midkiff 2018 recorded stories, Holzknecht 1985 PARADISEC audio.

sources.citation: Midkiff, David and Michelle (Shelly) Midkiff (compilers). 2019-. Middle Kodut (Watut) Dictionary. SIL International, Webonary (SIL archive 85273; 4,160 entries, work in progress).https://www.webonary.org/middlewatut/
sources.note: 'Phonology' page is a grapheme-phoneme table only (20 letters incl. prenasalised mp nt nts ngk, lateral flap l/r, glottal stop '); 'Grammar' page reads 'Forthcoming..'; no PDF available; entries have no pronunciation field and no stress marks. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Carter, John, John Grummitt, Janell Masters and Brian Paris. 2014. A sociolinguistic survey of the Watut languages: South Watut [mcy], Middle Watut [mpl], and North Watut [una]. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2014-006. Dallas: SIL International. 87 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.5 (pp. 12-13) reproduces Holzknecht's Middle Watut consonant chart (Table 7, '1989:54') and explicitly declines to analyse phonology; App. C 170-item IPA wordlists for Madzim/Babuaf, Marauna, Bencheng, Dungutung and Singono carry no stress marks (0 primary-stress marks in the text). Silent on stress. Sec. 2.4 lists all prior work (Fischer 1963, Hooley 1965 ms, Hooley 1971, Holzknecht 1989, Landweer & Reitmaier 1990 ms).

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: ANU. viii+228 pp. doi 10.15144/PL-C115 (hdl 1885/145647)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026 .H64 1989
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.7 Middle Watut, printed p. 54 (p. 62): Table 4.8 phoneme inventory plus two notes (r~l allophony; prothetic vowel between consonants across word boundaries, citing Fischer 1963:210). No statement on stress or accent. Ch. 4 intro (p. 50): 'brief phonological statement.. Full phonological statements are to be published at a later date'. The word 'stress' occurs only in unrelated places (p. 26 folk-perceived dialect differences 'intonation, stress, or speed of delivery'; Duwet note 11; sec. 4.6.23 SWT/NWT glottal 'through stress rules', no rule given).

sources.note: Sec. 4.2.7 Middle Watut (scan p. 106): same Table 4.8 and notes as the 1989 book; no stress statement.
